title: Tasks under a feature, and where removed things come back
subtitle: Every field editable, and anything removed can be found and restored

decisions.name: Tasks under a feature
decisions.question: How does a person add, change, set the status of and drop a task inside the feature panel?
decisions.common: The Tasks part of the one feature panel, everywhere it opens (Roadmap, Priorities, Home). Each row keeps its title, owner, due date and status; the heading counts what is done. Whoever can decide on the feature saves; an approver who is not its decider, or a commenter, proposes; a viewer reads. A proposed change waits under Proposals on it, worded as the change ('Add the task “Send a test digest to the support team”'). Every change shows a toast with Undo. A dropped task leaves the list and goes to Settings › Trash, where it is restored from.

proposals.name: Edit each row in place
proposals.what: Each part of a row is a control where it sits, like the panel's other fields: click the title to retitle it, the owner to pick a person, the date to pick a day; the status pill opens To do, Doing, Done and, last, Drop this task. A small '+ Add a task' row at the end opens one line to type in.
proposals.why: It works the way every other field in the panel already works, so there is nothing new to learn, and each change is one click and one save.
proposals.plus: Fastest for one change; owner and date are one click; the list keeps its reading shape.
proposals.cost: Every row carries a status picker, so the list reads busier; dropping sits inside the status picker, where it is less obvious.

proposals.name: Checklist with a tick
proposals.what: Tasks are a checklist: the tick marks a task done (and untick puts it back to do). A row's menu holds Mark as doing (Mark as to do on a task in progress), Change the title, Change owner or due date and Drop this task. An 'Add a task' box always waits at the end.
proposals.plus: The most common change, done, is one tick; done tasks are struck through so what is left stands out.
proposals.cost: Owner, date and doing hide behind a menu; a tick cannot say 'doing', so that state lives in a small tag.

proposals.name: Row menu and a form
proposals.what: Rows read as they do today. Each has a menu: Change…, Mark as to do / doing / done, Drop this task. Change and 'Add a task' open one small form with the title, owner and due date, saved together.
proposals.plus: The list stays as calm as now; a new task gets its owner and date in one go.
proposals.cost: Two to three clicks for any change, even a status; the form pushes the rows below it down.

proposals.name: Edit the whole list
proposals.what: An 'Edit tasks' button turns the list into a table of fields (task, owner, due, status) with 'Add a row'; 'Save all' sends every changed row at once, Cancel drops them.
proposals.plus: Good for a big tidy-up after a meeting: many tasks changed in one pass.
proposals.cost: A mode to enter and leave for one small change; long titles are cut short in the narrow Task column while editing; Save all sends several changes but the toast names only one.

decisions.name: Where removed things come back
decisions.question: Where does a person find a cut feature, an archived goal or a removed goal milestone, and bring it back?
decisions.common: Settled on Nov 4: Delete goes to Settings › Trash (restorable); Cut (feature) and Archive (goal) stay for 'not now'; the feature panel's own Cut, Restore and Delete live in its header menu, drawn in another set. This decision is only where cut features, archived goals and removed milestones come back. Each removed thing says what it was, where it was, who removed it and when (month first), with Restore. Whoever can decide on the feature saves; an approver who is not its decider, or a commenter, proposes; a viewer reads. The Undo toast stays as it is.

proposals.name: Show removed switch
proposals.what: A 'Show removed · N' switch under the Roadmap's filters (and the same on Priorities for archived goals). On, the page lists what was removed from it: its own cut features and its goals' removed milestones, each with Restore.
proposals.plus: Found where the thing used to be; nothing new in the menus.
proposals.cost: Each page needs its own switch and list; archived goals are not on any roadmap page; a dashed list pushes the timeline down.

frames.caption: At rest: 'Show removed · 2' under the Alerts roadmap's filters.

A commenter (Theo Brandt): each row reads Propose restoring.
A viewer: the list with no buttons.

proposals.name: Settings › Trash
proposals.what: Settings › Trash gets a second list, 'Removed from plans', under deleted documents: cut features, archived goals and removed milestones, filtered by kind, each with Restore. Deleted plan items stay in the Deleted list above, with its days left.
proposals.plus: One place for everything that left, the same place as deleted documents.
proposals.cost: Far from the plan; Trash is for owners only, so approvers and commenters cannot restore or propose from it; cut and archived are 'not now', yet they sit in Trash.

proposals.name: Removed list, panel says who
proposals.what: A 'Removed · N' button at the start of the Roadmap's filter row opens one list of everything removed from the plans (features, goals, milestones) with who and when, each with Restore. A cut feature opened from the list says 'Cut on Oct 21 by Priya Raman' under its title; its own Restore is in the panel header's menu (another set draws it).
proposals.why: Everything is found from the plan in one click, restored right there in the list, and the page stays clean until asked.
proposals.plus: One list for all three kinds; the count and the list drop the restored thing at once.
proposals.cost: One more button in the filter row; a list across all roadmaps grows long, so it scrolls.
